$comment: The Vapor mark, pinned. Single source of truth for the app (src/components/VaporMark.tsx) and the icon exporter (scripts/export-mark.mjs), so a rendered icon and the running logo can never drift apart. Values are the ones the 'Ribbon Mark Lab' study renders at — the <vapor-ribbon> element's own fallbacks differ (turns 1.5, curl 0.85) and would quietly draw a different logo.
$pose: Seconds into the idle animation. The renderer is deterministic, so this number IS the logo: same pose, same drawing, forever. 0 is the reference pose — the V with the hooked upper-left tip and the slightly elongated left arm. Legibility at 16px does not constrain this choice; the plate does that. Change it and re-run `npm run mark`, then `npx tauri icon brand/icon-1024.png`. `npm run mark -- --contact-sheet` renders the menu.

icon.$comment: Icon plate. A glass mark has no intrinsic contrast — it is only visible by what it refracts — so with no plate it washes out on an unknown background. White is the default because a macOS icon sits in a row of light, shaded tiles and a dark slab reads as a hole in that row. iOS additionally forbids alpha in app icons, so a plate is required there.
icon.$inset: Margin between plate edge and the mark's bounding box, as a fraction of the side.
icon.$markTheme: Which environment the glass refracts, NOT the background it sits on. The dark environment renders a deeper, more saturated ribbon, which is what holds contrast against a white plate; the light environment refracts near-white and disappears into it.
